_comment: ZENIT HYPERTUNE update manifest - repo root. App polls the raw URL once per day. sha256 = SHA256 of the setup exe; sig = Ed25519 signature over this manifest (signing.py). The app trusts a manifest only with a valid signature - without one it offers nothing, because url and sha256 come from the same unsigned file and would otherwise vouch for each other.
notes:
### A diagnosis that no longer kills the app - and a stale engine that no longer wins

#### Fixed
- **The "Export diagnostics" button no longer ends the app.** A customer machine (Intel, 20.10.2026) reported the same thing for the third time in a different shape: click the button, the window is gone, no traceback, not one line in `crash_log.txt`. That is the signature of `QThread: Destroyed while thread is still running` — Qt ends the process with `qFatal`, without a Python exception, so nothing can log it. Cause: `_diag_done` dropped the last reference to the worker while `run()` had not yet returned (it emits its signal at the end of `run`, not after it). The reference is now dropped on `finished` and the object deleted there — for the export **and** for the upload. The "busy" guard asks `isRunning()` instead of "is there an object", so a worker that has finished cannot lock the next export forever.
- **The two probes that reach into foreign code run in a child process now.** `limiter_status.txt` goes through NVAPI into the graphics driver (DRS profiles) and `game_mode_probe.txt` uses Win32 window/process queries. A native access violation in either killed the process before Python could turn it into an exception — a `try/except` in the caller can never catch that. Both now run via `--subtool diagprobe` in their own process: a crash lands in the zip with the child's exit code and reason, and the window stays. There is deliberately **no** fallback into the parent process (the reason for the isolation is that this call can kill it) and a 120 s timeout is recorded as a finding instead of being retried.
- **The isolated probe writes UTF-8 itself.** Found in this release's own suite run, not on a customer machine: the child printed with the console's code page (cp1252 on German Windows) while the parent read UTF-8, so `game_mode_probe.txt` carried `UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode characters ... position 412-413` instead of the probe. `diag_export.cli_entry` now sets its stdout/stderr to UTF-8 (`errors="replace"`) before the first character. The zip also records the command that produced each probe (`aufruf:`); that line was built but never printed, because the success and crash branches rebuilt the header without it.
- **The engine contract checks the signature, not three names.** On that same machine 15 steps reported `TypeError: get_hardware_runner() got an unexpected keyword argument 'read_only'`, next to `AttributeError: module 'imod' has no attribute 'apply_realtek_ndis_registry_guard'`. Both together do not mean "wrong argument" — they mean an **old engine** was answering under the name `imod`, one built before the read-only path existed. The old contract asked for three attribute names, and an old engine has all three and still fails at every later call. `hardware_leser` now requires `read_only` in the signature (`**kwargs` counts; an unreadable signature is not punished, so a compiled function is not rejected on suspicion).
- **In the built EXE the compiled engine wins over a leftover source file.** `entry._lade_engine` and `hardware_leser` preferred `IMOD-Test.py` sitting next to the EXE — so an old source copy left behind by an earlier source installation replaced the engine that shipped in the build. `crash_entry.txt` on the customer machine named exactly that file: `C:\Program Files\Hypertune\IMOD-Test.py`. In a frozen build the compiled module is used and the file is only the last resort; on a developer machine the file stays first, so a change is visible without a build. The developer path and the shipped path are now the only two, and each is checked by name.
- **26 subprocess calls in eight modules have a text path for bad bytes.** `sc qc`/`sc query`, `wevtutil el`, `powercfg -import`, `reg import`, the BAT output and the S.U.C.K. chain read with `text=True` and no encoding, i.e. with the ANSI code page. A single byte outside that page — `0x81`, entirely normal in the output of a German Windows build — ended the reader thread: nine times in the customer log, `UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x81 ... position 635`. The caller then received neither text nor an error, just a gap that looked like "the tool said nothing". All of them now pass `encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"`.
- **A failed driver check at startup is shown instead of ending the app silently.** `entry.py` imports `security_guard` as its first own module, and that module verifies the pinned `WinRing0x64.dll`/`WinRing0.sys` **at import** — before `main()` and therefore before any code that can open a dialog, in an EXE built without a console. Measured on a copy of the release tree with `chiptool/WinRing0x64.dll` removed: exit code 1, no window, no dialog, indistinguishable from "the app does not start at all". The import is now guarded by `_boot_fatal`, which writes the traceback to `crash_entry.txt` and shows a message box naming the reason.

#### Verified
- The full suite (`tests/run_all.py`): 185 suites, 3476 assertions, 0 red, 0 hanging, 0 crashes after a green line. `tests/test_diag_probe_isolation.py` contributes 19 of them (new in this release): the isolation contract, the engine signature, the compiled-engine precedence, a source-text contract for the worker lifetime (the reference must not be dropped in the result slot) and the text path of every touched subprocess call.
- The full suite (`tests/run_all.py`) and the build's own gates — sterility scan, replay of the built artifact, engine dispatch, network-tweaker backend — run for this release; their verdicts are in `_release_summary.txt` and the build log next to it.
- **Not verified:** the customer's Intel machine. The isolation and the reference lifetime are measured in tests and in the build; whether the button now produces a complete zip *on that machine* can only be confirmed by the zip it sends back.

#### Release
- **This build is unsigned**, as 8.6.29 and 8.6.30 were: neither the executable nor the two bundled DLLs carry a code signature, and the build marks its own artifact `Hypertune_Setup-unsigned.exe` until that changes. Windows SmartScreen will ask for confirmation.
- Please verify the SHA-256 of the installer and the signature of the manifest against the release page before installing.
